A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRAP research, with matching authors, core attack framework and principal experiments. The complete main texts and Appendices A–D support comparison, including figures, tables and equations.

before.justification: V1 reports original intervention experiments, simulated attacks on three VLAs, transferability and robustness analyses, and 15 physical robot trials.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds occlusion experiments, camouflage analyses, physical deployment tests and a defense evaluation.

M1.justification: V2 adds reference-image content regularization, CNN-based Deep Image Prior patch generation, and a CLIP-guided alternative (Section 5.3 and Appendix C.6). Section 7 implements format-specific consistency defenses where v1 only proposed a detector. These substantially extend the method; TV regularization, homography, color calibration and the core CoT/action losses already existed.

E1.justification: SimplerEnv, LIBERO and their curated tasks are retained. Coverage expands to simulated patch occlusion, physical tablecloth deployments with objects covering the patch, lighting and clutter variations, and a mouse-to-scissors physical scenario. V2 also evaluates the distinct task of detecting instruction–CoT inconsistency.

E2.justification: The main attack comparator set is unchanged: Action-Only becomes Action Attack, and CoT-Only becomes TRAPCoT-only. V2 adds GPT-5 as an evaluated comparator for the lightweight defenses in Table 6 and introduces a physical PGD-versus-DIP comparison.

E3.justification: V2 introduces center/edge occlusion tests at 10%, 25% and 50%, a TV-weight sweep, a 57 × 43 cm physical tablecloth setting, and defense metrics for benign consistency, attack rejection and latency. Table 9 revises and expands each instruction-variant set from four prompts to five. The stated 175-rollout unit changes from per VLA to per task; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine occlusion location and severity, PGD versus DIP camouflage, CLIP-guided textures, TV-weight sensitivity, and physical robustness to layouts, distractors and lighting (Appendices C.4, C.6 and D.3–D.5). The universal-patch study, latent-feature analysis and original failure cases are retained through relocation or renumbering.

E5.justification: V2 specifies 50 trials per optimizer for the new object-occluded physical comparison, supplementing the unchanged 15-trial original test and five simulation repeats. This adds trial-count information for a distinct experiment, rather than documenting increased repetitions of the old study. Table 1 dispersion reporting is unchanged, with no new confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 and the original physical outcomes remain unchanged. Table 4 replaces instruction-variant results under revised prompts: paraphrasing ASR changes from 53.6% to 70.6% for MolmoAct and 15.7% to 25.1% for InstructVLA, so these are not same-setting gains. New physical results report 19/50 successes for PGD and 17/50 for DIP; defense, occlusion and TV-regularization results substantially expand the evidence.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation expands the optimization objective and defines reference-feature and CLIP alignment losses (v2 Equations 4, 9 and 13). Existing CoT/action losses, homography and trajectory-score definitions remain substantively unchanged. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the introduction and conclusion's broad first-targeted-attack claim to CoT-based targeted behavior hijacking in reasoning VLAs. It also claims visually plausible physical patches. The central contribution—redirecting actions through adversarial manipulation of CoT without changing user instructions—remains intact.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the claim that object keywords alone trigger attacks with a context-dependent interpretation and adds hypotheses about reasoning format and CoT-to-action coupling. It interprets camouflage/effectiveness tradeoffs and occlusion sensitivity, and replaces the unaddressed-stealth limitation with transferability limitations. These substantially refine the account of practical applicability and failure conditions.

D1.justification: V2 documents physical content/TV weights of 1.5 and 100, an annealed DIP regularization strategy, global/local CLIP processing, and the larger tablecloth dimensions. It adds a project-page link advertised as hosting videos. Existing hardware and calibration-network details remain; v1's explicit randomized-homography EoT description is shortened.

R1.justification: V2 adds Deep Image Prior and TPatch citations, removes the Qi et al. visual-jailbreak reference, and narrows novelty positioning to CoT-based behavior hijacking. The pi0.5 and VLA-OS reference changes concern the same works with updated bibliographic information, rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 polishes terminology and prose, regroups method subsections into attack effectiveness and stealthiness, moves universal-patch analysis to Appendix C.5, and separates physical deployments into dedicated subsections. The principal section sequence and much existing exposition are retained; the expansion primarily adds scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the opening threat cartoon with a detailed framework overview, revises the physical-deployment figure, and adds optimizer, CLIP, deployment-variation and hazardous-task illustrations. New defense, occlusion and TV tables substantially expand the displays. Existing distribution, latent-feature, calibration and physical-result figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly left stealth unaddressed and only suggested a countermeasure. V2 substantially strengthens practical validation through patterned patches tested under physical occlusion, quantified sensitivity analyses, and an implemented defense comparison (Sections 5.3, 6.5 and 7; Appendices C–D). Revised instruction prompts also remove task-changing examples. Camouflage assessment remains largely visual and defense implementation details are limited, but the additions address important gaps in applicability and mitigation evidence without depending on higher headline scores.
